```{r}
#| include: false
blue <- "#4a7fb5"; amber <- "#e0902b"; red <- "#b2182b"; green <- "#1b7837"; grey <- "grey40"

# Synthetic control weights: min ||y1 - Y0 w||^2 on the simplex (accelerated projected gradient)
sc_weights <- function(y1, Y0, iters = 20000) {
  J <- ncol(Y0); A <- crossprod(Y0); b <- crossprod(Y0, y1)
  L <- max(eigen(A, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values)
  proj <- function(v) {
    u <- sort(v, TRUE); s <- cumsum(u); r <- max(which(u * seq_along(u) > s - 1))
    pmax(v - (s[r] - 1) / r, 0)
  }
  w <- z <- rep(1 / J, J); k <- 1
  for (i in 1:iters) {
    wn <- proj(z - (A %*% z - b) / L); kn <- (1 + sqrt(1 + 4 * k^2)) / 2
    z <- wn + (k - 1) / kn * (wn - w); w <- wn; k <- kn
  }
  drop(w)
}

# Ridge ASCM weights (Ben-Michael, Feller, Rothstein 2021, Lemma 1), pre-period columns centered
ascm_w <- function(y1, Y0, w, kappa) {
  X <- t(Y0 - rowMeans(Y0))
  drop(w + X %*% solve(crossprod(X) + kappa * diag(nrow(Y0)), y1 - Y0 %*% w))
}

# Simulated panel: 30 donors, 40 periods, two factors, effect ramps up after T0 = 28
J <- 30; TT <- 40; T0 <- 28
pre <- 1:T0; post <- (T0 + 1):TT
tau <- c(rep(0, T0), 0.25 * (1:(TT - T0)))
make_f <- function() {
  set.seed(8358)
  f1 <- 0.12 * (1:TT) + as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = .6), TT, sd = .25))
  f2 <- 1.5 * sin((1:TT) / 3.5) + as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = .6), TT, sd = .25))
  cbind(f1, f2)
}
sim <- function(mu1, F = make_f(), seed = 11, sd_e = .2) {
  set.seed(seed)
  mu <- rbind(mu1, cbind(runif(J, -1, 1), runif(J, -1, 1)))
  delta <- 0.5 + 0.03 * (1:TT)
  Y0 <- matrix(delta, TT, J + 1) + F %*% t(mu) + matrix(rnorm(TT * (J + 1), sd = sd_e), TT)
  Y <- Y0; Y[, 1] <- Y0[, 1] + tau
  list(Y = Y, Y0 = Y0, mu = mu, F = F)
}
est <- function(s) {
  y1 <- s$Y[pre, 1]; D <- s$Y[, -1]; w <- sc_weights(y1, D[pre, ])
  sc <- drop(D %*% w); did <- rowMeans(D) + mean(y1) - mean(rowMeans(D)[pre])
  att <- function(a) mean(s$Y[post, 1] - a[post])
  rmse <- function(a) sqrt(mean((y1 - a[pre])^2))
  list(w = w, sc = sc, did = did, att_sc = att(sc), att_did = att(did),
       rmse_sc = rmse(sc), rmse_did = rmse(did))
}
att_true <- mean(tau[post])

inside <- sim(c(.55, .5));  e_in <- est(inside)   # treated unit inside the donors' hull
outside <- sim(c(1.9, 1.7)); e_out <- est(outside) # treated unit outside the hull

# Dormant factor: f2 tracks f1 before T0, then falls away
F_dorm <- make_f()
F_dorm[pre, 2] <- F_dorm[pre, 1]
F_dorm[post, 2] <- F_dorm[T0, 1] + cumsum(rep(-.6, TT - T0))
dormant <- sim(c(1, 0), F = F_dorm, sd_e = .1); e_dorm <- est(dormant)
mu_dorm <- colSums(e_dorm$w * dormant$mu[-1, ])

# Ridge ASCM on the outside-hull case; penalty by holding out the last 8 pre-periods
y1_out <- outside$Y[pre, 1]; D_out <- outside$Y[, -1]
tr_p <- 1:20; ho_p <- 21:T0; kgrid <- 10^seq(-1, 4, .25)
cv_k <- sapply(kgrid, function(k) {
  w <- sc_weights(y1_out[tr_p], D_out[tr_p, ], 5000)
  wa <- ascm_w(y1_out[tr_p], D_out[tr_p, ], w, k)
  mean((y1_out[ho_p] - D_out[ho_p, ] %*% wa)^2)
})
kappa_hat <- kgrid[which.min(cv_k)]
w_asc <- ascm_w(y1_out, D_out[pre, ], e_out$w, kappa_hat)
asc <- drop(D_out %*% w_asc)
att_asc <- mean(outside$Y[post, 1] - asc[post])
rmse_asc <- sqrt(mean((y1_out - asc[pre])^2))

# Backdating: pretend treatment at t = 20 in the inside-hull case
fake <- 20
w_bd <- sc_weights(inside$Y[1:fake, 1], inside$Y[1:fake, -1])
gap_bd <- inside$Y[, 1] - drop(inside$Y[, -1] %*% w_bd)

# Plot helpers
yrange <- function(...) range(c(...))
traj_panel <- function(s, cf, cf_col = blue, cf_lab = "Synthetic control", main = "", leg = "topleft") {
  matplot(s$Y[, -1], type = "l", lty = 1, col = adjustcolor(grey, 0.2), las = 1, main = main,
          ylim = yrange(s$Y[, -1], s$Y[, 1], cf, s$Y0[, 1]), xlab = "Period", ylab = "Y")
  abline(v = T0 + .5, lty = 3)
  lines(s$Y0[, 1], col = amber, lwd = 2.5, lty = 3)
  lines(cf, col = cf_col, lwd = 2.5, lty = 2)
  lines(s$Y[, 1], col = red, lwd = 3)
  legend(leg, c("Treated", "True Y(0)", cf_lab, "Donors"),
         col = c(red, amber, cf_col, adjustcolor(grey, 0.5)), lty = c(1, 3, 2, 1), lwd = c(3, 2.5, 2.5, 1), bty = "n")
}
hull_panel <- function(s, w, main = "Loadings") {
  m <- s$mu[-1, ]; lim <- range(s$mu) + c(-.1, .1)
  plot(m, pch = 16, col = adjustcolor(grey, 0.5), las = 1, xlim = lim, ylim = lim, main = main,
       xlab = expression(mu[1]), ylab = expression(mu[2]), cex = 1)
  h <- chull(m); polygon(m[h, ], border = grey, lty = 2)
  points(m, pch = 1, col = blue, cex = 7 * sqrt(w), lwd = 2)
  points(s$mu[1, 1], s$mu[1, 2], pch = 8, col = red, cex = 1.8, lwd = 2.5)
}
```

```{r}
#| include: false
#| cache: true
# Basque Country: Abadie and Gardeazabal (2003) specification via Synth
library(Synth)
data(basque)
fit_b <- function(tr, ctl) {
  dp <- dataprep(
    foo = basque,
    predictors = c("school.illit", "school.prim", "school.med", "school.high", "school.post.high", "invest"),
    predictors.op = "mean", time.predictors.prior = 1964:1969,
    special.predictors = list(
      list("gdpcap", 1960:1969, "mean"),
      list("sec.agriculture", seq(1961, 1969, 2), "mean"),
      list("sec.energy", seq(1961, 1969, 2), "mean"),
      list("sec.industry", seq(1961, 1969, 2), "mean"),
      list("sec.construction", seq(1961, 1969, 2), "mean"),
      list("sec.services.venta", seq(1961, 1969, 2), "mean"),
      list("sec.services.nonventa", seq(1961, 1969, 2), "mean"),
      list("popdens", 1969, "mean")),
    dependent = "gdpcap", unit.variable = "regionno", unit.names.variable = "regionname",
    time.variable = "year", treatment.identifier = tr, controls.identifier = ctl,
    time.optimize.ssr = 1960:1969, time.plot = 1955:1997)
  invisible(capture.output(so <- synth(data.prep.obj = dp, method = "BFGS")))
  list(dp = dp, so = so)
}
gap_of <- function(f) drop(f$dp$Y1plot - f$dp$Y0plot %*% f$so$solution.w)
yr <- 1955:1997
rmspe_ratio <- function(g) sqrt(mean(g[yr > 1969]^2)) / sqrt(mean(g[yr <= 1969]^2))

donors <- c(2:16, 18)
bq <- fit_b(17, donors)
bq_gap <- gap_of(bq)

# Placebos: every donor treated in turn, Basque Country kept in the pool (as in ADH 2010)
pl <- lapply(donors, function(d) fit_b(d, setdiff(c(17, donors), d)))
pl_gap <- sapply(pl, gap_of)

# Leave-one-out for the two positive-weight donors
loo_cat <- gap_of(fit_b(17, setdiff(donors, 10)))
loo_mad <- gap_of(fit_b(17, setdiff(donors, 14)))
```

```{r}
#| include: false
reg_names <- basque$regionname[match(donors, basque$regionno)]
short <- function(x) sub(" \\(.*", "", x)
bq_w <- setNames(drop(bq$so$solution.w), short(reg_names))
bq_syn <- drop(bq$dp$Y0plot %*% bq$so$solution.w); bq_y <- drop(bq$dp$Y1plot)
ratios <- c("Basque" = rmspe_ratio(bq_gap), setNames(apply(pl_gap, 2, rmspe_ratio), short(reg_names)))
p_bq <- mean(ratios >= ratios["Basque"])
spain <- basque$gdpcap[basque$regionno == 1]
gdp60 <- c(basque = mean(bq_y[yr %in% 1960:1969]), spain = mean(spain[yr %in% 1960:1969]))
```

## Plan for today

When can a weighted combination of untreated units stand in for the counterfactual?

1. Identification: the factor model
2. Estimation: weights, the convex hull, comparison to DiD
3. Inference with one treated unit
4. Failure modes and practice
5. Many treated units: interactive FEs, matrix completion, SDID

## From DiD

- DiD imputes $Y_{1t}(0)$ from the average donor change
- Requires parallel trends
- Imputation (L9): fit $Y(0)$ on untreated cells, predict the rest

. . .

Today: same imputation, weaker restriction on $Y(0)$, one treated unit.

# Block 1: Identification

## One treated unit

- One unit, treated at a known date
- Several untreated units
- Target: the **path** of effects for that unit

. . .

Abadie and Gardeazabal (2003): ETA terrorism and Basque GDP. Donors: 16 other Spanish regions.

## Setup

Abadie, Diamond, and Hainmueller (ADH 2010):

- Units $j \in \{1, \dots, J+1\}$, periods $t \in \{1, \dots, T\}$
- $Y_{jt} = Y_{jt}(0) + D_{jt}\tau_{jt}$
- Unit 1 treated: $D_{1t} = \mathbf{1}\{t > T_0\}$
- Donors: $D_{jt} = 0$ for all $t$, $j \geq 2$

. . .

Target, for $t > T_0$:

$$
\tau_{1t} = Y_{1t} - \underbrace{Y_{1t}(0)}_{\text{unobserved}}
$$

## Basque Country vs. Spain

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11

plot(yr, bq_y, type = "l", col = red, lwd = 3, las = 1, ylim = range(bq_y, spain),
     xlab = "Year", ylab = "GDP per capita (1986 USD, 000s)")
lines(yr, spain, col = grey, lwd = 3)
abline(v = 1969.5, lty = 3)
legend("topleft", c("Basque Country", "Spain"), col = c(red, grey), lwd = 3, bty = "n")
```

1960s GDP per capita: `r sprintf("%.2f", gdp60["basque"])` vs. `r sprintf("%.2f", gdp60["spain"])`. Different levels, different structure before ETA.

## Factor model

$$
Y_{jt}(0) = \delta_t + \theta_t X_j + \lambda_t \mu_j + \varepsilon_{jt}
$$

- $\delta_t$: common shock
- $X_j$: observed covariates, $\theta_t$ time-varying coefficients
- $\lambda_t$: $R$ unobserved common factors
- $\mu_j$: unobserved loadings
- $\varepsilon_{jt}$: mean-zero shocks

. . .

$\lambda_t = \lambda$ and $\theta_t = \theta$: unit FE, parallel trends.

Otherwise units load differently on common shocks. Requires $T_0 > R$.

## Factors and loadings: an example

Stylized, not estimated. Units are states, the outcome is unemployment, one factor ($R = 1$).

$$
Y_{jt}(0) = \delta_t + \lambda_t \mu_j + \varepsilon_{jt}
$$

- **Factor** $\lambda_t$: the national manufacturing cycle. One number per year, the same for every state: high in a boom, low in a bust.
- **Loading** $\mu_j$: how exposed state $j$ is to that cycle. Michigan (industrial) has a large $\mu_j$; Massachusetts (mostly services) has a small one.
- **Shock** $\varepsilon_{jt}$: everything else that hits one state in one year, such as a plant closing or a policy change.

. . .

Michigan is treated. Weighting service states fails: when the cycle turns, they barely move and Michigan does. We need donors whose **weighted loading** $\sum_j w_j \mu_j$ matches Michigan's $\mu_1$.

That can be Ohio and Indiana, or a mix of one very exposed and one barely exposed state: loadings 2 and 0 with weights $(\tfrac12, \tfrac12)$ give a weighted loading of 1.

. . .

Neither $\lambda_t$ nor $\mu_j$ is observed. If the weighted donors track Michigan's pre-period path through booms and busts, that is evidence the exposures match.

## Parallel trends fails in the simulation

$J = 30$, $T = 40$, $T_0 = 28$, $R = 2$, effect ramps to 3. Treated loadings $(0.55, 0.50)$, not the donor mean.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11

par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 1, 1), cex = 1.25)
traj_panel(inside, e_in$did, cf_col = green, cf_lab = "DiD")
```

DiD pre-period RMSE `r sprintf("%.2f", e_in$rmse_did)`. ATT `r sprintf("%.2f", e_in$att_did)`; truth `r sprintf("%.2f", att_true)`.

## Balancing weights

Unit 1 is treated; donors are $j = 2, \dots, J+1$. Every sum over $j$ below runs over donors. Weights: $w = (w_2, \dots, w_{J+1})$, $w_j \geq 0$, $\sum_{j=2}^{J+1} w_j = 1$.

Treated unit, untreated outcome:

$$
Y_{1t}(0) = \delta_t + \theta_t X_1 + \lambda_t \mu_1 + \varepsilon_{1t}
$$

Weighted donors (using $\sum_j w_j = 1$):

$$
\sum_{j=2}^{J+1} w_j Y_{jt} = \delta_t + \theta_t \sum_{j=2}^{J+1} w_j X_j + \lambda_t \sum_{j=2}^{J+1} w_j \mu_j + \sum_{j=2}^{J+1} w_j \varepsilon_{jt}
$$

. . .

The target is the gap between the two. We choose $w$ so the pre-period gap is zero.

## What cancels

Suppose for all $t \leq T_0$: $\sum_{j=2}^{J+1} w_j Y_{jt} = Y_{1t}$, and $\sum_{j=2}^{J+1} w_j X_j = X_1$.

Subtract the weighted donors from the treated unit:

$$
Y_{1t}(0) - \sum_{j=2}^{J+1} w_j Y_{jt} = \theta_t \Big( X_1 - \sum_j w_j X_j \Big) + \lambda_t \Big( \mu_1 - \sum_j w_j \mu_j \Big) + \Big( \varepsilon_{1t} - \sum_j w_j \varepsilon_{jt} \Big)
$$

- $\delta_t$ cancels: it is common to every unit, and the weights sum to one
- $X$ term is zero: the second condition makes it identical on both sides, whatever $\theta_t$ is
- $\mu$ term balances only approximately: the fit is on $Y$, which includes $\varepsilon$

. . .

In the pre-period the left side is zero by construction, so $\lambda_t (\mu_1 - \sum_j w_j \mu_j) = -(\varepsilon_{1t} - \sum_j w_j \varepsilon_{jt})$: the loading imbalance is as large as the noise the fit absorbed.

## Bias bound

With exact fit and $T_0 > R$, for $t > T_0$:

$$
Y_{1t}(0) - \sum_{j=2}^{J+1} w_j Y_{jt} = \sum_{j=2}^{J+1} w_j \sum_{s=1}^{T_0} \psi_{st} (\varepsilon_{js} - \varepsilon_{1s}) - \sum_{j=2}^{J+1} w_j (\varepsilon_{jt} - \varepsilon_{1t})
$$

$$
\psi_{st} = \lambda_t \Big( \sum_{n=1}^{T_0} \lambda_n' \lambda_n \Big)^{-1} \lambda_s'
$$

- First term: vanishes in $T_0$, relative to the scale of $\varepsilon$
- Second term: mean zero
- Bound grows with $J$ and $R$ (Abadie 2021)

# Block 2: Estimation

## The estimator

For $t > T_0$:

$$
\hat\tau_{1t} = Y_{1t} - \sum_{j=2}^{J+1} \hat w_j Y_{jt}
$$

Exact balance requires $(Y_{11}, \dots, Y_{1T_0}, X_1)$ in the convex hull of the donors.

Otherwise minimize imbalance.

## Choosing $w$ and $V$

$\mathbf{X}_1$, $\mathbf{X}_0$: predictors, including summaries of pre-period outcomes.

$$
\hat w(V) = \arg\min_{w \in \Delta} (\mathbf{X}_1 - \mathbf{X}_0 w)' V (\mathbf{X}_1 - \mathbf{X}_0 w)
$$

$V$ diagonal, non-negative. Data-driven choices:

- Minimize pre-period outcome MSPE (ADH 2010)
- Cross-validate on train and validation periods (ADH 2015)

## Inside the hull

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.6
layout(matrix(1:2, 1), widths = c(2.1, 1))
par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 2, 1), cex = 1.15)
traj_panel(inside, e_in$sc, main = "Outcomes")
hull_panel(inside, e_in$w)
```

Pre-period RMSE `r sprintf("%.2f", e_in$rmse_sc)`. ATT `r sprintf("%.2f", e_in$att_sc)`; truth `r sprintf("%.2f", att_true)`. Circles: $\hat w_j$, sparse. Star: treated.

## Outside the hull

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.6
layout(matrix(1:2, 1), widths = c(2.1, 1))
par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 2, 1), cex = 1.15)
traj_panel(outside, e_out$sc, main = "Outcomes")
hull_panel(outside, e_out$w)
```

Pre-period RMSE `r sprintf("%.2f", e_out$rmse_sc)`. ATT `r sprintf("%.2f", e_out$att_sc)`; truth `r sprintf("%.2f", att_true)`. All weight on `r sum(e_out$w > .01)` donor.

## Synth vs. DiD

| | DiD | Synth |
|---|---|---|
| $\hat Y_{1t}(0)$ | $\hat\alpha + \frac{1}{J} \sum_{j=2}^{J+1} Y_{jt}$ | $\sum_{j=2}^{J+1} \hat w_j Y_{jt}$ |
| Weights | uniform | convex, data-driven |
| Intercept | yes | no |
| $Y(0)$ | parallel trends | interactive FE |
| Beyond donors | extrapolates (level shift) | interpolates (convex hull) |

Simulation, truth `r sprintf("%.2f", att_true)`:

| | DiD | Synth |
|---|---|---|
| Inside the hull | `r sprintf("%.2f", e_in$att_did)` | `r sprintf("%.2f", e_in$att_sc)` |
| Outside the hull | `r sprintf("%.2f", e_out$att_did)` | `r sprintf("%.2f", e_out$att_sc)` |

## Exercise

$j = 1$ treated at $T_0 = 4$; donors $j = 2, 3, 4$.

| | $t=1$ | $t=2$ | $t=3$ | $t=4$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $Y_{1t}$ | 5 | 7 | 6 | 8 |
| $Y_{2t}$ | 4 | 6 | 5 | 7 |
| $Y_{3t}$ | 6 | 8 | 7 | 9 |
| $Y_{4t}$ | 3 | 5 | 8 | 6 |

(a) Write the SC problem for $w$ with all pre-period outcomes as predictors, $V = I$.

(b) If $Y_{1t} = (2, 2, 2, 2)$, does an exact $w$ exist?

(c) Compute synth and DiD estimates of $Y_{1,5}(0)$ when $Y_{2,5} = 8$, $Y_{3,5} = 10$, $Y_{4,5} = 7$. Why do they differ?

::: {.notes}
(a) min over the simplex of sum_t (Y_1t - sum_j w_j Y_jt)^2.
Exact solution, unique: w = (1/2, 1/2, 0).
(b) No. Every donor is at least 3 in every period, so 2 is outside the hull.
(c) Synth: 0.5(8) + 0.5(10) = 9. DiD: alpha-hat = 6.5 - 6.167 = 0.333; donor mean at t = 5 is 8.333; DiD = 8.667. DiD gives unit 4 weight 1/3 even though its pre-period path differs.
:::

# Block 3: Inference

## The problem

- Trends treated as fixed
- Uncertainty: error in the approximation of $Y_{1t}(0)$
- $N_1 = 1$: no averaging over treated units

## Placebo test

ADH (2010): apply SC to each donor as if treated.

$$
r_j = \frac{\text{RMSPE}_j(T_0 + 1, \dots, T)}{\text{RMSPE}_j(1, \dots, T_0)}, \qquad
p = \frac{1}{J+1} \sum_{j=1}^{J+1} \mathbf{1}\{r_j \geq r_1\}
$$

- Exact under exchangeable assignment
- Minimum $p$: $1/(J+1)$

## Placebos: Basque Country

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.5
layout(matrix(1:2, 1), widths = c(1.5, 1))
par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 2, 1), cex = 1.1)
matplot(yr, pl_gap, type = "l", lty = 1, col = adjustcolor(grey, 0.4), las = 1, main = "Gaps",
        xlab = "Year", ylab = "Actual - synthetic", ylim = range(pl_gap, bq_gap))
lines(yr, bq_gap, col = red, lwd = 3); abline(h = 0, col = grey); abline(v = 1969.5, lty = 3)
o <- sort(ratios)
par(mar = c(4, 9, 2, 1))
plot(o, seq_along(o), pch = 19, col = ifelse(names(o) == "Basque", red, grey), yaxt = "n", ylab = "",
     xlab = "Post/pre RMSPE", main = "Ratios", xlim = c(0, max(o)))
axis(2, at = seq_along(o), labels = names(o), las = 1, cex.axis = 0.7)
```

$p =$ `r sprintf("%.2f", p_bq)`. Minimum possible: $1/17 \approx$ `r sprintf("%.3f", 1/17)`. Basque Country stays in each placebo pool, as in ADH.

## Hahn and Shi (2017)

- Permutation validity requires symmetry
- Repeated-sampling view: symmetry generally fails; size distorted (Monte Carlo)
- Randomization view (Abadie): symmetry built in by assumption

. . .

What is the $p$-value about: assignment, or sampling?

## Firpo and Possebom (2018)

- Placebo test: uniform assignment across units
- Parametric family of assignment probabilities; uniform is a special case
- Sensitivity of the decision to departures from uniform

## Conformal: Chernozhukov, Wüthrich, and Zhu (2021)

Under the sharp null $\tau_{1t} = 0$: fit on **all** periods, residuals $\hat u_t = Y_{1t} - \hat Y_{1t}(0)$.

$$
S_q(\hat u) = \Big( \frac{1}{\sqrt{T - T_0}} \sum_{t > T_0} |\hat u_t|^q \Big)^{1/q}
$$

- $q = \infty$: large transient effects; $q = 1, 2$: persistent effects
- iid permutations: exact under exchangeability of $\{u_t\}$
- Moving blocks: stationarity and weak dependence
- Works with DiD, SC, constrained Lasso, factor models, matrix completion
- CIs by test inversion
- Ignores weight estimation error (Cattaneo et al. 2021)

## Inference: summary

All need the factor model (or similar) for the estimator itself.

| Method | Additional assumption |
|---|---|
| Placebo (ADH 2010) | Exchangeable assignment |
| Conformal (Chernozhukov et al. 2021) | Stationary/exchangeable shocks |
| Prediction intervals (Cattaneo et al. 2021) | Moment conditions on estimation and shock errors |
| Subsampling (Li 2020) | Long panel |

# Block 4: Failure modes and practice

## Dormant factors

Hollingsworth and Wing (2022): factors collinear before $T_0$, distinct after. Treated $\mu = (1, 0)$.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.3
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4.5, 2, 1), cex = 1.15)
matplot(F_dorm, type = "l", lty = c(1, 2), lwd = 3, col = c(blue, amber), las = 1, main = "Factors",
        xlab = "Period", ylab = expression(lambda[t]))
abline(v = T0 + .5, lty = 3)
legend("bottomleft", c(expression(lambda[1]), expression(lambda[2])), col = c(blue, amber), lty = 1:2, lwd = 3, bty = "n")
traj_panel(dormant, e_dorm$sc, main = "Outcomes")
```

Pre-period RMSE `r sprintf("%.2f", e_dorm$rmse_sc)`. Weighted loadings $(`r sprintf("%.2f", mu_dorm[1])`, `r sprintf("%.2f", mu_dorm[2])`)$. ATT `r sprintf("%.2f", e_dorm$att_sc)`; truth `r sprintf("%.2f", att_true)`.

## Dormant factors: an example

Stylized, not estimated. Same setting as the factors and loadings example: Michigan is treated.

- Before $T_0$, one factor drives state unemployment: the manufacturing cycle $\lambda_{1t}$.
- After $T_0$, a second factor switches on: a sharp drop in oil prices, $\lambda_{2t}$. It barely moved before, so it contributed almost nothing to any state's outcome.
- States differ a lot in exposure $\mu_{j2}$: Michigan has little oil; Texas and North Dakota have a lot.

. . .

The weights pick Ohio, Indiana, and Texas, because their pre-period paths followed Michigan's through the manufacturing cycle. Nothing before $T_0$ revealed Texas's oil exposure.

When prices crash, Texas unemployment jumps, the synthetic Michigan jumps with it, and the gap reads as a policy effect that is really the oil shock.

. . .

- An excellent pre-period fit, and the weights are still wrong on the one dimension that mattered later.
- Not a violation of the factor model, which allows factors to switch on. The weights were fit on a period that gave them no chance to learn $\mu_{j2}$.
- Fix: choose donors on substantive knowledge of what could differ in exposure. Excluding oil states avoids it. The simulation above is the same problem: weighted loadings $(0.80, 0.20)$ against treated $(1, 0)$.

## Imperfect fit

Ferman and Pinto (2021). Without exact fit, $\hat w$ trades off:

- Matching loadings
- Minimizing variance of weighted shocks

. . .

- $\hat w$ does not recover the loadings, even as $T_0 \to \infty$
- Biased if assignment is correlated with the factors

. . .

Demeaned SC (add an intercept):

- Can improve on DiD in bias and variance
- Still biased under selection on time-varying factors

## Non-unique $W$

Abadie and L'Hour (2021):

- Inside the hull: many $w$ with the same fit
- Different $w$, different post-period estimates
- Near the boundary: corner solution, few donors

## Unstable $V$

Kuosmanen, Zhou, Eskelinen, and Malo (2021): Basque application, three algorithms.

| | Synth | MSCMT | Global optimum |
|---|---|---|---|
| $w$: Catalonia | 0.851 | 0.633 | 0 |
| $w$: Madrid | 0.149 | 0.148 | 0.441 |
| $w$: Baleares | 0 | 0.219 | 0.370 |
| $w$: La Rioja | 0 | 0 | 0.190 |
| $v$: GDP per capita | 0.201 | 0.999 | 1 |
| Pre-period $R^2$ | 0.969 | 0.985 | 0.985 |

- Bilevel problem; `Synth` numerically unstable
- Optimum typically a corner: all $V$ on one predictor
- Other predictors then irrelevant

## Donor pool and covariates

Abadie (2021):

- Exclude units with similar interventions or large idiosyncratic shocks
- Small, curated pool over large, heterogeneous one

Covariates:

- Omitted $X_j$ go into $\mu_j$: more factors, larger bound

Multiple outcomes:

- Reduce overfitting (Sun, Ben-Michael, and Feller 2025)

## Diagnostics

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.9
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4.5, 2, 1), cex = 1.15)
plot(yr, bq_gap, type = "l", col = red, lwd = 3, las = 1, main = "Leave-one-out: Basque Country",
     ylim = range(bq_gap, loo_cat, loo_mad), xlab = "Year", ylab = "Gap")
lines(yr, loo_cat, col = blue, lwd = 2.5, lty = 2); lines(yr, loo_mad, col = amber, lwd = 2.5, lty = 3)
abline(h = 0, col = grey); abline(v = 1969.5, lty = 3)
legend("bottomleft", c("All donors", "Drop Catalonia", "Drop Madrid"), col = c(red, blue, amber), lty = 1:3, lwd = 2.5, bty = "n")
plot(gap_bd, type = "l", col = red, lwd = 3, las = 1, main = "Backdating: simulation", xlab = "Period", ylab = "Gap")
abline(h = 0, col = grey); abline(v = fake + .5, lty = 2, col = blue); abline(v = T0 + .5, lty = 3)
text(fake + .5, max(gap_bd), "fake T0", col = blue, pos = 2)
```

- Report weights, predictor balance, pre-period gap
- Vary $V$ and the donor pool
- Effect large relative to outcome volatility (Abadie and Vives-i-Bastida 2022)

Mean gap: `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(bq_gap[yr > 1969]))`; drop Catalonia `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(loo_cat[yr > 1969]))`; drop Madrid `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(loo_mad[yr > 1969]))`.

## Augmented SCM

Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2021). Bias correction, as in matching (L3):

$$
\hat Y_{1T}^{\text{aug}}(0) = \sum_{j=2}^{J+1} \hat w_j Y_{jT} + \Big( \hat m_{1T} - \sum_{j=2}^{J+1} \hat w_j \hat m_{jT} \Big)
$$

$\hat m$: outcome model on pre-period outcomes. Ridge ASCM:

$$
\hat w_j^{\text{aug}} = \hat w_j + (X_1 - X_0' \hat w)' (X_0' X_0 + \kappa I)^{-1} X_j
$$

- $X_j$ centered; $\kappa$ sets the extrapolation
- Negative weights allowed
- Good fit: $\hat m$ correction small, ASCM $\approx$ SCM

## Ridge ASCM outside the hull

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.5
layout(matrix(1:2, 1), widths = c(2.1, 1))
par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 2, 1), cex = 1.15)
traj_panel(outside, asc, cf_col = green, cf_lab = "Ridge ASCM", main = "Outcomes")
plot(sort(w_asc), pch = 19, col = ifelse(sort(w_asc) < 0, red, blue), las = 1, main = "ASCM weights",
     xlab = "Donor (sorted)", ylab = "Weight")
abline(h = 0, col = grey)
```

| | Pre-period RMSE | ATT |
|---|---|---|
| SCM | `r sprintf("%.2f", e_out$rmse_sc)` | `r sprintf("%.2f", e_out$att_sc)` |
| Ridge ASCM | `r sprintf("%.2f", rmse_asc)` | `r sprintf("%.2f", att_asc)` |
| Truth | | `r sprintf("%.2f", att_true)` |

# Block 5: Many treated units

## Matrix view

$$
Y(0) = \begin{pmatrix} Y_{co,pre}(0) & Y_{co,post}(0) \\ Y_{tr,pre}(0) & \textbf{?} \end{pmatrix}
$$

$$
\text{ATT} = \frac{1}{N_1} \sum_{it: D_{it} = 1} \big( Y_{it} - \hat Y_{it}(0) \big)
$$

Fit on untreated cells, impute **?**, average (L9). Methods differ in the model for $\hat Y_{it}(0)$.

## Interactive FE: Xu (2017)

$$
Y_{it}(0) = X_{it}' \beta + \alpha_i + \xi_t + \mu_i' \lambda_t + \varepsilon_{it}
$$

Generalized synthetic control:

1. Estimate $\hat\beta, \hat\lambda_t, \hat\mu_{co}$ on controls (Bai 2009)
2. Estimate $\hat\mu_i$ for treated units on pre-period outcomes
3. Impute

- $R$ by cross-validation
- Consistent as $N_{co}, T_0 \to \infty$; suggested $N_{co} \geq 40$, $T_0 \geq 10$
- Strict exogeneity of $X_{it}$

## Matrix completion: Athey et al. (2021)

Same factor structure, $L$ low rank:

$$
\hat L = \arg\min_L \frac{1}{|\mathcal{O}|} \| P_{\mathcal{O}}(Y - L) \|_F^2 + \kappa \|L\|_*
$$

- $\|L\|_*$: sum of singular values
- Soft-thresholds rank, no fixed $R$; $\kappa$ by cross-validation

. . .

$$
\begin{pmatrix} 1 & ? \\ 4 & 8 \\ 3 & 6 \end{pmatrix}
\quad \Rightarrow \quad
\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 4 & 8 \\ 3 & 6 \end{pmatrix}
= (1, 4, 3)' (1, 2)
$$

## One objective

Athey et al. (2021):

$$
\min \frac{1}{|\mathcal{O}|} \big\| P_{\mathcal{O}}\big( Y - AB' - \alpha 1_T' - 1_N \xi' \big) \big\|_F^2
$$

| Method | Restriction |
|---|---|
| DiD | $AB' = 0$ |
| Synthetic control | $A$: non-negative columns summing to 1 |
| Interactive FE | Fixed rank $R$ |
| Matrix completion | Penalty $\kappa \| AB' \|_*$ |

## Exercise

Units 3 and 4 treated from $t = 3$:

$$
Y(0) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 4 & 8 \\ 3 & 6 & ? \\ 1 & 2 & ? \end{pmatrix}
$$

(a) Does $Y_{it}(0) = \alpha_i + \xi_t$ fit the observed cells?

(b) Does $Y_{it}(0) = \mu_i \lambda_t$? If so, impute.

(c) What does this imply for TWFE vs. interactive FE?

::: {.notes}
(a) No. Changes t=1 to t=2 are 1, 2, 3, 1: not parallel.
(b) Yes. mu = (1, 2, 3, 1), lambda = (1, 2, 4). Missing entries: 12 and 4.
(c) TWFE would impute from additive changes; the factor model fits exactly. Fit on the untreated cells can discriminate.
:::

## SCM with staggered adoption

Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2022). Treated unit $j$, imbalance $q_j$:

- $q^{sep}$: root mean of $q_j^2$
- $q^{pool}$: imbalance of the average pre-period gap

$$
\min_{\Gamma} \; \nu (\tilde q^{pool})^2 + (1 - \nu)(\tilde q^{sep})^2 + \kappa \|\Gamma\|_F^2
$$

- $\nu = 0$: separate; $\nu = 1$: pooled
- With intercept: weighted DiD

## Synthetic DiD: Arkhangelsky et al. (2021)

$$
\hat\tau^{sdid} = \arg\min_{\tau, \alpha, \xi, m} \sum_{i, t} (Y_{it} - m - \alpha_i - \xi_t - D_{it} \tau)^2 \, \hat\omega_i \hat\phi_t
$$

| | $\alpha_i$ | Unit weights | Time weights |
|---|---|---|---|
| DiD | yes | uniform | uniform |
| SC | no | $\hat\omega_i$ | none |
| SDID | yes | $\hat\omega_i$ | $\hat\phi_t$ |

- $\hat\omega_i$: regularized toward uniform
- $\hat\phi_t$: pre-periods that predict the post-period among controls
- Either set removes bias: approximately unbiased
- Inference: placebo, jackknife, block bootstrap

## Which method

| | Short $T_{pre}$ | Long $T_{pre}$ |
|---|---|---|
| **Many $N_{co}$** | TWFE imputation | Matrix completion, SDID |
| **Few $N_{co}$** | SDID or TWFE imputation; hard for all | GSC, SCM-based |

- Short $T_{pre}$ and interactive FE: incidental parameters
- Hold-out test: hide untreated periods, predict them (Liu, Wang, and Xu 2024)
- `fect`, `gsynth`, `augsynth`, `synthdid`

## Summary

- SC: weights balancing a factor model in pre-period outcomes
- Good fit is necessary, not sufficient (dormant factors)
- Outside the hull: SC fails; augmentation extrapolates
- Inference: placebos, conformal, intervals. One treated unit, strong assumptions
- Many units: same imputation, different $Y(0)$ models
